before:
The main airport for Belém, 12 km from downtown, and the gateway to the mouth of the Amazon. It is named after Júlio Cezar Ribeiro de Souza, a nineteenth century balloon researcher, a name it took in April 2010.

It has been run by the Consortium Novo Norte since it left Infraero in 2023.

Its history is transatlantic. Val de Cans began in the 1930s as a 1,200 metre earth strip. When the Second World War broke out, airports on the Brazilian coast became critical for moving aircraft, people and equipment across the South Atlantic to West Africa, and after negotiations between Brazil and the United States, proper concrete and asphalt runways were built here for the Air Transport Command. Thousands of aircraft built in Canada and the United States passed through on their way to North Africa and Europe.

Some facilities are shared with a Brazilian Air Force base.
after:
The main airport for Belém, 12 km from the city centre. Since April 2010 its official name has been Belém/Val-de-Cans/Júlio Cezar Ribeiro International Airport.

It has been run by the Novo Norte consortium, trading as NOA (Norte da Amazônia Airports), since it left Infraero in 2023. The military also uses the airfield.

Val de Cans began in the 1930s as a 1,200 metre earth strip. In the Second World War it became a stop on the route for new military aircraft flown from factories in Canada and the United States, and two concrete and asphalt runways were built for military flying.

claims.note: Belém has a second, smaller airport (renamed Brigadeiro Protásio de Oliveira by the same 2010 law); Val de Cans is the international one, and the operator calls it the largest airport terminal in the North region.

claims.note: Checked for a 2025 or 2026 change of operator: none. The consortium (Socicam and Dix) won the Bloco Norte II concession in August 2022; its company, SPE Novo Norte, trades as NOA and began operating in 2023 (Wikipedia: Infraero's figures run to August 2023, NOA's from September 2023). NOA's 2025 report (March 2026) still names Socicam and Dix as its owners, and DECEA's live entry names NOA. Wikipedia's infobox says NOA from 2022, which is the auction year.

Held back: the old text gives no traffic figure, so this replaces nothing. The operator's 2025 report says Belém passed 4 million passengers for the second time in its history (2024 and 2025), the largest airport terminal in the North region; Wikipedia's infobox gives 4,008,723 for 2025. The same report says works finished for COP30 in November 2025 raised capacity from 7.7 million to about 13 million a year, though the operator's own airport page still gives 7.7 million.
